FOR campaign/the-wanderers -- RED AT `gate`, one failure, and it is a real finding rather than a pin to move.

    sky_exit_criterion::moons_flip_the_calendar_and_seat_gods_no_moonless_world_can_hold
    cli/tests/suite/sky_exit_criterion.rs:275

    "moons must not retire a source kind a moonless sky already had:
       {ambient, celestial-body, wandering-star}
     is not a subset of
       {celestial-body, eclipse, tide, wandering-star}"

READ THE TWO SETS. A MOONLESS sky produces `ambient`. A sky WITH moons does not. Your change makes adding moons REMOVE a source kind, and the assertion exists precisely to forbid that: moons may add `eclipse` and `tide` — they do, both are there — but they must not take `ambient` away.

WHY THIS ONE IS CONSTITUTIONAL RATHER THAN A CALIBRATION. CLAUDE.md's provider-tier rule is that higher fidelity REFINES, never contradicts, lower — "coarse constrains fine". A moon-bearing sky is the finer model of the same world; if it drops a source the coarse model had, the refinement is contradicting rather than refining. That is the invariant this test encodes, and re-pinning it would retire the guarantee rather than record a readout.

So the question is where `ambient` went. Your diff touches anchor, calendar, ephemeris, lib, pins, provider, render and star — eight astronomy files — and the likeliest shapes are that the moon path builds its source set from scratch instead of extending the moonless one, or that a match arm on sky kind stopped falling through to the ambient case. Either produces exactly this: the added kinds present, one prior kind silently gone.

I WAS WRONG ABOUT WHICH ASSERTION WOULD FIRE, and should say so. I warned you to watch census_sentinel, because you touch 16 world files with no census. It did not fire at all — `grep -c census_sentinel` on your run is 0. The sentinel compares committed census VALUES; your change moved a structural property of the sky that a different, older exit criterion was watching. My reasoning about which guard was exposed was worse than the guard's own coverage.

FOR WHAT IT IS WORTH ON PROCESS: this is your branch's first contact with any gate — there is no stage row for campaign/the-wanderers in the queue's history — and the failure is 40 s into the `gate` phase of a merge that costs ~1900 s. A stage gate would have found it for the same 40 s and without holding a merge slot. Not a criticism of the work; just the cheaper order.

Main is unchanged. Nothing pushed.
